unitTitle: Adjectives/Order of Adjectives/Comparisons - Expressing Certainty - Will

pairsWith.noteUz: Bu nazariya beti Coursebook 3-unit (Shop till you Drop!) grammatikasini takrorlaydi: sifatlar, sifatlar tartibi, qiyoslash darajalari.

scanNote:
GRAMMAR 2, 3-UNIT NAZARIYA (14-bet, PDF 13). Yuqorida chapda ko'k '3', sarlavha: 'Adjectives/Order of Adjectives/Comparisons - Expressing Certainty - Will'. Och pushti ramka.

'Adjectives': • Adjectives describe nouns. They have the same form in the singular and plural. 'a red car - (two) red cars' • Adjectives go before nouns. 'a large box'. They can also be used alone after the verb to be and after verbs such as look, smell, sound, feel, taste etc. 'Mary is tall. You look sad. It smells horrible.' • There are two kinds of adjectives: opinion adjectives (e.g. beautiful, lovely, great, expensive, etc) which show what a person thinks of somebody or something, and fact adjectives (e.g. short, square, yellow, cotton, etc) which give us factual information about somebody or something (e.g. size, weight, colour, etc).

'Order of Adjectives': • Opinion adjectives go before fact adjectives. 'a beautiful silk scarf' • When there are two or more fact adjectives in a sentence, they usually go in the following order: JADVAL 'Fact Adjectives': size: small, big, short, long, etc; weight: heavy, light, etc; shape: triangular, round, rectangular, square, etc; colour: dark/light blue, yellow, pink, cream, red, purple, etc; material: cotton, leather, silk, plastic, woollen, nylon, metal, gold, silver, velvet, wooden, canvas, china, etc. • We do not usually have a long list of adjectives before a single noun. 'an expensive, red, leather suitcase'

'Comparisons' JADVALI: adjective / comparative / superlative. one-syllable adjectives: cheap - cheaper - the cheapest; large - larger - the largest; big - bigger - the biggest. -y adjectives: easy - easier - the easiest. adjectives with two or more syllables: intelligent - more intelligent - the most intelligent. irregular adjectives: good - better - the best; bad - worse - the worst; much/many - more - the most; little - less - the least; far - further/farther - the furthest/the farthest.

Bet raqami: pastda chapda '14'.

exercises.instructionEn: Adjectives describe nouns. They have the same form in the singular and plural: a red car - (two) red cars. Adjectives go before nouns: a large box. They can also be used alone after the verb to be and after verbs such as look, smell, sound, feel, taste etc: Mary is tall. You look sad. It smells horrible. There are two kinds of adjectives: opinion adjectives (e.g. beautiful, lovely, great, expensive) which show what a person thinks of somebody or something, and fact adjectives (e.g. short, square, yellow, cotton) which give us factual information (e.g. size, weight, colour, etc).
exercises.instructionUz: Sifatlar otlarni tasvirlaydi. Birlik va ko'plikda bir xil shakl: a red car - (two) red cars. Sifatlar otdan OLDIN keladi: a large box. Shuningdek, 'to be' va look, smell, sound, feel, taste kabi fe'llardan keyin yolg'iz ishlatiladi: Meri baland bo'yli. Sen xafa ko'rinasan. U yomon hidlanyapti. Sifatlar ikki xil: FIKR sifatlari (beautiful, lovely, great, expensive) - odamning fikrini bildiradi; FAKT sifatlari (short, square, yellow, cotton) - haqiqiy ma'lumot beradi (o'lcham, og'irlik, rang va h.k.).

exercises.instructionEn: Opinion adjectives go before fact adjectives: a beautiful silk scarf. When there are two or more fact adjectives in a sentence, they usually go in the following order: size (small, big, short, long), weight (heavy, light), shape (triangular, round, rectangular, square), colour (dark/light blue, yellow, pink, cream, red, purple), material (cotton, leather, silk, plastic, woollen, nylon, metal, gold, silver, velvet, wooden, canvas, china). We do not usually have a long list of adjectives before a single noun: an expensive, red, leather suitcase.
exercises.instructionUz: Fikr sifatlari fakt sifatlaridan OLDIN keladi: a beautiful silk scarf (chiroyli ipak ro'mol). Ikki yoki undan ko'p fakt sifati bo'lsa, tartib: o'lcham (small, big, short, long), og'irlik (heavy, light), shakl (triangular, round, rectangular, square), rang (dark/light blue, yellow, pink, cream, red, purple), material (cotton, leather, silk, plastic, woollen, nylon, metal, gold, silver, velvet, wooden, canvas, china). Odatda bitta otdan oldin uzun sifatlar ro'yxati bo'lmaydi: an expensive, red, leather suitcase.

exercises.instructionEn: One-syllable adjectives: cheap - cheaper - the cheapest; large - larger - the largest; big - bigger - the biggest. -y adjectives: easy - easier - the easiest. Adjectives with two or more syllables: intelligent - more intelligent - the most intelligent. Irregular adjectives: good - better - the best; bad - worse - the worst; much/many - more - the most; little - less - the least; far - further/farther - the furthest/the farthest.
exercises.instructionUz: Bir bo'g'inli sifatlar: cheap - cheaper - the cheapest; large - larger - the largest; big - bigger - the biggest. -y sifatlar: easy - easier - the easiest. Ikki va undan ko'p bo'g'inli sifatlar: intelligent - more intelligent - the most intelligent. Noto'g'ri sifatlar: good - better - the best; bad - worse - the worst; much/many - more - the most; little - less - the least; far - further/farther - the furthest/the farthest.
exercises.explanationUz:
QIYOSLASh - 3 DARAJA.

  ODDIY → QIYOSIY (-roq) →
  ORTTIRMA (eng)

  1) BIR BO'G'INLI: -er / the -est
     cheap → cheapER → the
       cheapEST
     large → largER → the largEST
       (-e bor - faqat -r/-st)
     big → biGGer → the biGGest
       (undosh ikkilanadi)

  2) -Y BILAN TUGAYDIGAN: -y → -ier
     / the -iest
     easy → easIER → the easIEST

  3) IKKI+ BO'G'INLI: more / the
     most
     intelligent → MORE intelligent
       → THE MOST intelligent

  4) NOTO'G'RI (yodlash):
     good → better → the best
     bad → worse → the worst
     much/many → more → the most
     little → less → the least
     far → further/farther → the
       furthest/farthest


⚠ ORTTIRMADA 'THE' ShART:

  'the cheapest' (cheapest ✗).


⚠ 'MORE CHEAPER' ✗:

  Yo -er, yo more - ikkalasi emas.
